note: The last unextracted half of each civilization entity: its building-library bindings and its four preconfigured settlement plans. Resolved from the Python civilization registry at FantasyWorldGenerator b67c99b after validate_registry() passed. Every entity in civilizations.json carries exactly ten keys -- population (-> civilizations.json), settlement, economy, sky, presentation (-> entity-rules.json), and the five here: buildings, small_city, medium_city, capital_city, hamlet. With this file the entity is whole. ORDER IS A CONTRACT, the same one entity-rules.json states: this list is the registry's `civilization_order`, which is what terrain_profiles.civilization_ids() returns and what the lab colours regions by. Append, never insert. `buildings.packs` MAPS A PACK ID TO THE OPTION IDS THIS PEOPLE MAY BUILD, and both the pack ids and the option ids are keys into buildings.json. Every entity must bind the fallback pack (city_pack_generic_surface) or the loader refuses the registry, and every entity must list `rural` in structure_block_ids or the same. These bindings are read as SETS -- building_pack_data turns them into option.profiles lists and terrain_settlements turns those straight back into set() -- so the order of the id lists inside `packs` and `layout_features` is free. No entity binds the `castle` library; castle_planner reaches it directly. THE PLAN LISTS ARE ORDER-SENSITIVE, WITHOUT ANY RNG. city_planner and hamlet_planner walk `buildings` in list order, split into core-priority and the rest, and greedily install each row into the FIRST free candidate plot, stamping a positional id (plot-0, plot-1, ...). Reordering a plan list therefore moves buildings onto different plots, renumbers every plot id, and can change WHICH rows fail to place when the site runs out of terrain-safe ground. Append, never insert. Each row is merged over its structure record as {**structure, **row}, so the row's name and count win and the structure supplies dimensions_m, plot_m, staffing, priority and geometry_type. `placement_conditions` are drawn from an eighteen-value closed set in civilization_registry.PLACEMENT_CONDITIONS; an unknown one is refused at load. THE REGISTRY IDENTITY IS ORDER-SENSITIVE DOWN TO OBJECT KEYS, which is why `source_key_order` is recorded below. registry_identity() is sha256(json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',',':'))) with NO sort_keys, over the MERGED document, and that digest is written into world.civilizations.registry, world.city_plans.identity.registry and world.hamlet_plans.identity.registry, and re-checked before an age advance -- so reordering any key in civilizations.json or buildings.json retires every saved world even when no value changed. `source_key_order.hashed_document` is the top-level key order of the document that is hashed: the raw civilizations.json keys in file order, then `entities` (the flattened civilization_order map, each entity being its raw block with parent_race_id appended last), then the four building sections, then building_catalogue_metadata; `parent_races` is replaced in place by {race: {name, founding_participation_percent}}. A port that wants to RECOMPUTE that digest rather than trust the recorded one must reassemble the document in exactly that order from these shards. `source_identity` records the expected value, and `source_document_header` carries the five top-level values of civilizations.json that no other extracted file kept, so that reassembly is possible at all: with them, plus registry-sections.json (defaults, city_classification, parent_races, founding_rules), civilizations.json (population per entity, and the one aggregate `configurations` entry, which is the profile with id "mixed"), entity-rules.json, this file and buildings.json, every key of the hashed document is accounted for. `building_catalogue` is the sibling-file link the loader insists on; it is the path that made buildings.json a separate file and is not a second copy of anything.

source_document_header.description: Single authoring source for independent civilizations, generic rule parameters, presentation, building/layout libraries and measured structure blocks. No population inheritance.
